CONDITION_A.description: Original query plus mode-specific answer contract only; no LegalRetrievalResult evidence, no corpus metadata, no E-style evidence IDs.

CONDITION_B.description: LegalQueryUnderstanding plus frozen top-5 LegalAI retrieval evidence using the existing grounded prompt and citation contract.

component_hash_changes.reason: Bug fix: model_unavailable_result() referenced undefined http_status, provider_code and provider_message and raised NameError whenever the answer model was unavailable (missing key or model), so the API returned QUERY_PIPELINE_UNAVAILABLE instead of MODEL_UNAVAILABLE. Its provider_diagnostic now records None for them (no provider was called). Prompt, schemas, parsing and citation validation are unchanged; already-generated eval outputs keep their recorded run hashes.

Output limit and truncation (step 11c): GeminiAnswerAdapter sends generationConfig.maxOutputTokens (LEGALAI_LLM_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, default 2048) and raises GEMINI_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED on finishReason MAX_TOKENS; ModelGenerationMetadata gains finish_reason and prompt_version. Prompt v1, schemas, parsing and citation validation are unchanged.

New prompt v2 for the product runtime (step 11c): mandatory structured claims tied to evidence IDs, case names copied exactly, and a no-coverage answer when no evidence is relevant. Prompt v1 (legal_answer_prompt.py, 5a300bf8...) stays the frozen baseline of this evaluation and its pin is unchanged.

Provider limits (step 11d): GeminiAnswerAdapter sends generationConfig.thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel (LEGALAI_GEMINI_THINKING, default low) and uses LEGALAI_GEMINI_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (default 90); records thoughtsTokenCount; logs sanitized provider error type/code/message for non-2xx responses. ModelGenerationMetadata gains reasoning_tokens and evidence_items_trimmed. Prompt v1, schemas, parsing and citation validation are unchanged.

Provider label fix (step 22): model_provider_failure_result() hard-coded provider="gemini" in the failure metadata of every unanswered request, whatever the provider. generate_legal_answer now passes the failed provider, read from the error code prefix (failed_provider_name: GROQ_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED -> groq, NVIDIA_TIMEOUT -> nvidia); the parameter defaults to "gemini", so the frozen evaluation path (run_grounded_answer_eval_generation.py, Gemini only) records the same as before. Prompt v1, schemas, parsing and citation validation are unchanged; already-generated eval outputs keep their recorded run hashes.

New prompt v3 for the product runtime (step 22): prompt v2 unchanged plus length rules (about 900 output tokens public, 1,200 professional; no repetition; short lists; citations only in claims, with source_metadata limited to case_name and source_url; no P# citations; the private document map not restated), so professional answers and briefs fit Groq's 8,000-token per-request limit. Same output schemas. Prompt v1 (the frozen baseline of this evaluation) and v2 keep their pins.

rubric.quality_composite_formula: mean(LEGAL_RELEVANCE, LEGAL_CORRECTNESS, GROUNDING_SUPPORT, CITATION_QUALITY, COMPLETENESS, UNCERTAINTY_HANDLING, REGIME_HANDLING, ACTIONABILITY)
